reference: Diethyl N-(tert-butoxycarbonyl)phosphoramidate: a new, useful substitute of phthalimide in Gabriel-type syntheses of primary amines | Zwierzak, Andrzej; Pilichowska, Slawomira | Synthesis (1982), (11), 922-4
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Diethyl N-Alkyl-N-(t-butoxycarbonyl)-phosphoramidates (6); General Procedure: A mixture of sodium derivative 4 (5.50 g, 0.02 mol), the alkyl bromide (5; 0.02 mol), tetrabutylaminium bromide (0.64 g, 0.002 mol), and benzene (25 ml) is refluxed with stirring for 3 h. The product is cooled to room temperature, diluted with benzene (25 ml), and treated with water (10 ml) to dissolve sodium bromide. The organic layer is separated and washed with water (3 × 10 ml). The washings are reextracted with benzene (3 × 10 ml) and the extracts arc combined with the organic layer. The extract is dried with magnesium sulfate and evaporated and the residue heated at 30-40 °C/1-2 torr for 1 h to give either spectroscopically pure (1H- and 31P-N.M.R.) 6 (a-i) or 6 (j, k, l) contaminated with unreacted 3. Diethyl N-Alkyl-N-(t-butoxycarbonyl)-phosphoramidates (6k). Yield: 36%. The reaction was carried out in boiling acetonitrile for 6 h. The product was isolated after evaporation of acetonitrile and replacing it by benzene. As determined by 31P-N.M.R. spectrometry, the crude product is a mixture of 6k (69%) and 3 (31%). 31P-N.M.R. 24.3 MHz (CCl4/85% H3PO4ext): δ [ppm]: 0.20.
